sibling_release_windows.semantics: Independent observed JOIN episodes, not all workload JOINs. Actual allocator release uses scheduler wall time; complete JOIN uses the existing client-clock offset conversion. Only explicitly identified dynamic subagents link by workflow/parent context/JOIN. Host-only or post-JOIN releases cannot support pre-JOIN H2D. A command qualifies only with the existing proof of actual pre-JOIN submission and FULL reuse by the following request. Temporal association does not prove exclusive capacity, child-to-parent page identity, that these bytes were necessary for prefetch, or a native-relative saving. Cumulative releases are not simultaneously free capacity; transferred FULL bytes are command receipts, not a count of unique pages. Unobserved JOIN completion leaves the release window unknown.

parent_handoff_observations.semantics: Actual terminal-suffix allocator release, linked to the first observed completed parent GPU batch, not kernel start; RETURN delivery observation and service observation use scheduler wall time, not client event time; not exclusive slot ownership, predictive H2D reuse, avoided D2H bytes, or a native-relative latency saving. Restore lookahead is selection evidence, not submission/ACK evidence. Aggregate releases include internal calls; scope breakdown and terminal_children use explicit invocation-create metadata or recorded runtime scope, never ID spelling. Only confirmed dynamic subagents link to JOIN parent services; absent metadata stays unknown. Missing pool byte sizes stay unknown.

summary.semantics: Release bytes are actual cumulative allocator releases, not simultaneous occupancy, avoided transfers, exclusive parent capacity, or JCT savings. Only explicit invocation-create metadata or recorded runtime scope classify contexts; conflicting evidence stays separate. Scheduler terminal-observation timestamps are used for release delay; client event clocks are not subtracted. A last recorded pending-anchor count is not a live backlog: retries with no release need not emit records. The terminal_context_cache_sample event is also emitted on ordinary context-epoch invalidation: its name does not prove an invocation RETURN. Retired checkpoint counts are not returned-agent counts. The matched subset shares the exact workflow/invocation/context/epoch/session key of an observed terminal release; only its separately counted later records postdate that scheduler terminal observation. Earlier matching samples are not post-terminal occupancy. Missing release evidence remains unproven. Ancestry includes shared prefixes and protected state; its per-context distributions are neither globally additive nor a measurement of exclusively dead/reclaimable bytes. Missing runtime instrumentation is unavailable evidence, never zero native lifecycle cost. Transfers lack the node creation/session ownership needed to prove bytes sent after a terminal boundary; no such avoided-DMA estimate is made.
